name: PointBase
tagline: Pure-Java embeddable SQL database once bundled with the J2EE SDK and WebLogic; long discontinued.
description: PointBase was a small relational database written entirely in Java, started in 1998 by Oracle co-founder Bruce Scott with Jeff Richey and Daren Race. It ran in-process or as a lightweight server through JDBC, and became familiar to a generation of Java developers because Sun shipped it with the J2EE SDK and BEA bundled it with WebLogic as a development database. DataMirror bought it in 2003, IBM bought DataMirror in 2007, and the product quietly disappeared; later WebLogic releases switched to Apache Derby. Today it only matters when you inherit an old Java EE sample app or test fixture that expects it.
statusNote: Acquired by DataMirror (2003), which IBM bought in 2007; PointBase is no longer sold or supported. Use Apache Derby, H2 or HSQLDB.

pricing.notes: Historically licensed commercially; free copies shipped only for development inside the J2EE SDK and WebLogic. No longer sold.

scale.notes: A development and embedded database; bundled evaluation copies were capped at small database sizes.

strengths: Zero-install pure-Java engine that ran wherever a JVM did
Shipped with the J2EE SDK and WebLogic, so many old tutorials and samples assume it
Embedded and client-server modes behind the same JDBC interface
weaknesses: Discontinued for well over a decade; no downloads, patches or support
Bundled copies were licensed for development and testing only
No modern JDBC, Java module or SQL feature support
useCases: Reading or porting legacy J2EE and WebLogic sample applications
Understanding the history of embedded Java databases
